description: A stack reads its column with a plain coercion and adds the result to a running cursor, and **nothing is substituted for what that comes to**: `v = +field(t); if (v < 0) { t[y0] = lastNeg; t[y1] = lastNeg += v } else { t[y0] = lastPos; t[y1] = lastPos += v }`. A `NaN` is not less than zero, so it takes the positive branch and poisons the cursor — that row gets a `y0` and no `y1`, and every row after it in the same group gets neither. The totals behave the same way, `partition` summing `Math.abs(field(g[i]))` with no guard of its own. This engine answered `0` for a value it could not read, which is not a missing piece of a chart but a different chart: the segment was drawn flat on the baseline and the rest of the stack carried on as though nothing had happened. The first group holds a word among its numbers and the second holds the same rows without it, so the fixture says both what is poisoned and what is not; the third is a column of **only** unreadable values, whose stack sums to `NaN` and whose axis therefore has no ticks at all — a scale of `[NaN, NaN]` positions nothing, which is what upstream draws and what a fallback to `[0, 0]` quietly replaces with an axis nobody asked for.
